description:
`log` records what an app you authorize did for one of your enrollments ("checked 214 listings, 3 matched") in that enrollment's activity log, and, only if you also allow it, reads the log back.

The gateway answers `log` itself (`log://enrollment`): there is no upstream. A write is one entry `{"level", "message", "attributes"}` or an array of up to 100; the gateway validates them, stamps your account, the enrollment and its own receipt time, and records them; you read them under the enrollment's **Activity** in the dashboard. The enrollment is named by the `X-UnitySVC-Enrollment` header and must be one your key may see. `log` holds your own data, so its exports declare two permissions and nothing else: `write` records entries and `read` lists them. `invoke`, and the `service:*` and `*` wildcards that stand for it, never reach `log`. A grant's `log_level` option is the lowest level it records (`debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`, default `debug`): entries below it are dropped and counted as `dropped` in the answer. Entries are kept 90 days. `log` is not billed.

`POST /log` with a UnitySVC key whose policy grants `service:log` with `write`, e.g. `{"object": "service:log", "permissions": ["write"], "options": "log_level=info"}`, and the header `X-UnitySVC-Enrollment: <code>`; the answer is `202 {"accepted": n, "dropped": m, "entry_ids": [...]}`. `GET /log` with the same header and a key that holds `read` lists the newest entries first, filtered by `level`, `since`, `until` and `limit`, and paged by passing the answer's `next_cursor` back as `before`.

log_level.description: The lowest level this grant records: entries below it are dropped. Unset records every level.
log_level.title: Lowest level recorded

name: log

payout_price.description: Not billed: recording and reading your own activity log is free

summary: Let an app record what it did for one of your enrollments in that enrollment's activity log through `/log`, and read it back only if you also allow it.
